topIssues.title: daily-codegen failing since 2026-11-05: invalid GITHUB_TOKEN_GOVERNANCE, and failure Slack alert broken
topIssues.author: sbvegan
topIssues.body:
## Summary

Since 2026-11-05, the `daily-codegen` CircleCI job has failed on every day that it detected on-chain drift. No automated codegen PR has been opened since #1393 (2026-10-30). The failure alert that should have flagged this is also broken, so the job has been failing silently.

## Root cause 1: `GITHUB_TOKEN_GOVERNANCE` is invalid

Codegen runs and commits fine. The **Create PR to update codegen files** step then fails on `git push`:

```
remote: Invalid username or token. Password authentication is not supported for Git operations.
fatal: Authentication failed for 'https://github.com/***.git/'
```

The token in the `circleci-repo-superchain-registry` context appears to have expired or been revoked between 2026-10-30 (last successful push) and 2026-11-05 (first failure).

Runs that show the error (`circleci run get <id> --failure-report`):
- 2026-11-05: `d39093ac-bc31-46ad-b6a9-dc2e61055b23`
- 2026-11-12: `2d8f94c7-1f74-4b5c-b022-c000ff6ca324`
- 2026-11-18: `9b1543f4-6688-47cd-9b9e-4ae7eacfeed2`

On days with no drift, the job halts early and reports success. That is why the history is mixed:

| Dates | Result | Drift present? |
|---|---|---|
| Nov 3–4 | ✅ | No |
| Nov 5–12 | ❌ | Yes (caught up manually in #1409) |
| Nov 13–16 | ✅ | No |
| Nov 17–18+ | ❌ | Yes (OP Mainnet proposer, Soneium mainnet roles) |

## Root cause 2: the failure alert can't send

The `slack/notify` step (`event: fail`, #notify-ci, @protocol-oncall) errors with:

```
In order to use the Slack Orb (v4 +), an OAuth token must be present via the SLACK_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable.
```

Neither of the job's contexts (`circleci-repo-superchain-registry`, `circleci-repo-rpc-secrets`) provides `SLACK_ACCESS_TOKEN`. The success notification uses `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` instead, which is why it still works. `daily-check-review-period-delays` uses the same `slack/notify` setup and contexts, so its failure alerts are probably broken too.

## Fix

- [ ] Rotate `GITHUB_TOKEN_GOVERNANCE` (`opgitgovernance`) with branch push and PR create permissions on this repo, and update it in the `circleci-repo-superchain-registry` context
- [ ] Make `SLACK_ACCESS_TOKEN` available to `daily-codegen` and `daily-check-review-period-delays`, either by adding it to that context or by adding the org context that already holds it
- [ ] Re-run with `daily_codegen_dispatch=true` and confirm a PR is opened. Do this while drift exists, otherwise the push step is skipped and the token isn't tested.

## Related

- #1416 and #1418 manually applied drift (OP Mainnet proposer, Soneium mainnet roles) that this job would normally have caught.

topPRs.title: sepolia-devnets: add op-int-0 and uni-int-0 in one interop dependency set
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds the two new OP Labs staging replicas, deployed fresh at op-contracts v9.0.0 on 18 Nov 2026 (devnets-private#2723, #2724), in a new `sepolia-devnets` superchain dir.

| Chain | Chain ID | Replicates | Block time | Dependency set | Lagoon |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| op-int-0 | 420130023 | OP Sepolia | 2s | 420130023 + 420130024 | 30 Nov 2026 16:00:01 UTC (`1796054401`) |
| uni-int-0 | 420130024 | Unichain Sepolia | 1s | 420130023 + 420130024 | 30 Nov 2026 16:00:01 UTC (`1796054401`) |

- Both chains are in one interop dependency set.
- The Lagoon time matches sepolia-devnet-2, -3 and -6.
- SuperchainConfig is `0x289d2A1b1AE6E0470D8B72E53B6E3f485f251DBb`, the one the other OP Labs Sepolia devnets use.

## Additive only

Nothing existing is moved or renamed, so no running network, node image or Kubernetes manifest is affected. The directory restructure for sepolia-devnet-2 to -5 stays in #1414 and can be reviewed separately.

## Notes

- Chain configs were written from the committed `rollup.json` and `state.json`; genesis files are the op-deployer `inspect genesis` output. `import-devnet` could not be used because a prepare/continue deployment has no `appliedIntent` in its state file.
- `addresses.json`, `chainList.*` and `CHAINS.md` regenerated with `codegen --superchains sepolia-devnets` (reads L1). Both chains report `permissionless`.
- Each chain still has its own DisputeGameFactory. The shared one comes with `OPCM.migrate`, as in #1412.

## Testing

- `check_genesis_integrity`, `check_depsets`, `check_chainlist`: pass
- `apply_hardforks`: no diff
- `go test ./internal/manage/ ./internal/config/`: pass

topPRs.title: ops: reject unknown keys when decoding registry TOML
topPRs.author: geoknee
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #1403. This is the follow-up it recommends.

## What

The ops tooling decoded registry TOML leniently. A key the Go structs don't model was silently dropped, and then lost when the config was rewritten on promotion. That is how #1398 got through: a staged `minBaseFee` passed `sync_staging --check` with `validation successful` and disappeared, while every downstream consumer (op-core, kona) decodes strictly.

After this PR, an unknown key fails the read and names the key:

```
failed to read .../.staging/wch-sepolia.toml: unknown TOML keys not represented in the target struct: genesis.system_config.minBaseFee
```

## Changes

- `paths.ReadTOMLFile` decodes with op-service's `jsonutil.DecodeTOMLStrict`, which the registry already uses for hardforks validation. It covers staged chain configs, staged and shipped `superchain.toml`, and the standard config params.
- The remaining direct `toml.Unmarshal` readers of registry configs use the same strict decode: `manage.CollectChainConfigs`, `manage.ReadChainConfig` and `paths.SuperchainIds`. That covers shipped configs too, so a key added by hand under `superchain/configs/` is caught.
- `config.SuperchainDefinition` gains `safer_safes_addr`, which `mainnet`/`sepolia` `superchain.toml` have carried since #1197. op-core already models it; the registry's own struct didn't. Nil pointers aren't encoded, and `WriteSuperchainDefinition` never overwrites an existing file, so generated output doesn't change.
- Removed a stale `deployment_tx_hash` from the `testchain.toml` test fixture. It's a staging-only field that shipped configs never have.

## Verification

- `TestConfigReadersRejectUnknownKeys` and `TestReadTOMLFile_RejectsUnknownKeys` fail on the #1403 base and pass here. They cover the decoder and each reader: staged chain, staged superchain, collected chain configs, and chain config by name.
- `TestShippedConfigsDecodeStrictly` strictly decodes every shipped `superchain.toml` and chain config (7 superchains, 63 chains). It fails with `safer_safes_addr` when that field is removed.
- `apply_hardforks` rewrites everything through the strict path with no diff. `check-chainlist` and `check-genesis-integrity` pass. Both `standard-config-params-*.toml` decode strictly into `validation.ConfigParams`.
- Replayed every staged config ever committed on a PR branch that I have locally (29 versions). The 2025 drafts carried keys the schema no longer has (`superchain_level`, `hardforks.interop_time`, `regolith_time`, roles under `[addresses]`, `protocol_versions_addr`), all of which were silently dropped. The most recent, `wch-sepolia` (2026-11), is the #1398 `minBaseFee` case. On this stack it decodes cleanly; without #1403 it is rejected.
- `go vet ./...` is clean. Local golangci-lint can't load the Go 1.26 module (the pinned 1.64.8 is a Go 1.23 build), so lint is left to CI. `TestBinaryInvocation`, `TestScanL2` and `TestVersionsIntegrity` need RPC and cache env vars, so they run in CI only.

## Merge order

Merge after #1403. Without it, staged configs that set the new genesis fields are rejected. That is the intended behaviour, but it would block chains that need them.

topPRs.title: ops: build against upstream go-ethereum
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
`ops` drops its op-geth `replace` and builds against upstream go-ethereum v1.17.10. The monorepo pin moves to [`8ec68e48a36c`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/commit/8ec68e48a36c4f8dfc6cb84e85d9a35d0ac60792), a develop commit after ethereum-optimism/optimism#24176, which moved the monorepo itself off op-geth. No module in this repo depends on op-geth any more.

No call site needed adapting: #1382, #1383 and #1384 already moved `ops` to op-core's genesis and chain config types and to opaque genesis files. `check_genesis_integrity` prints the same result for every chain before and after.

One change besides `go.mod`: the mock JSON-RPC server in `internal/testutil/mockrpc` sent `"error": null` in every success response. go-ethereum v1.17.10's client reads any `error` member as an error (ethereum/go-ethereum#36151), so the mock now omits it unless the call failed, as JSON-RPC 2.0 requires.

Notes for review:

- All RPC reads in `ops` target L1, so no read can hit an L2 deposit transaction, which upstream go-ethereum cannot decode.
- The pion modules that op-geth carried in patched versions now resolve to newer versions through upstream, and only a dependency's tests reach them.
- `govulncheck` reports no new finding; three findings in `klauspost/compress` and `golang.org/x/net` go away with the raised versions.
- CI runs the RPC-backed tests (`TestScanL2`, `TestVersionsIntegrity`, `TestBinaryInvocation`) and the full `codegen` check on this bump. Not exercised: `sync_staging` and `print_staging_report` beyond their early exit, because no chain is staged here.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.2*

topPRs.title: docs: update registry consumers and stale repo docs
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
op-geth is end of life: it doesn't implement Karst, which is active on mainnet and sepolia, so the docs shouldn't point chain operators at `op-geth --op-network`. The README, CONTRIBUTING and hardfork-inheritance docs now name the clients that embed the registry today (op-node, kona-node, op-reth) and their network flags.

The second commit fixes other stale statements in the same docs:

- CONTRIBUTING described a `superchain` Go module, a top-level `go.work` and a YAML superchain config, none of which exist. It now describes the `superchain` directory, the `validation` module and the TOML superchain config as they are.
- The "CheckSecurityConfigs" and "CircleCI Checks" sections are deleted: the test and the CI jobs they describe are gone and nothing replaces them.
- Dead links into docs.optimism.io and a step-numbering gap in `docs/ops.md` are fixed.

topPRs.title: mainnet, sepolia: Add OP and Unichain interop dependency set
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
OP Mainnet and Unichain activate Lagoon together, and so do OP Sepolia and Unichain Sepolia. This PR puts each pair in one interop dependency set. Each chain lists both chain IDs under `[interop.dependencies]`.

The dependency set controls the Lagoon activation. op-node and kona add the `setFeature(INTEROP)` deposit and the `ETHLiquidity` funding deposit only when the set has more than one chain. Without this change, nodes and the kona prestate treat each chain as a one-chain set. Lagoon then activates without the interop predeploys.

`check_depsets` passes. `apply-hardforks` and `codegen` produce no other diff.

After `lagoon_time`, `check_depsets` also requires both chains in a set to have the same `DisputeGameFactoryProxy` and `EthLockboxProxy`. The two chains in each pair do not share these addresses yet. So `addresses.json` must get the shared addresses before activation (10 Dec 2026 for Sepolia), or CI fails after that time.
